subject: Medisys: Request for peak-load SLA addendum & order form exhibit
messages:
From: Sophia Li <sophia@medisys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Reynolds <andrew.reynolds@medisys.com>, Karen Miles <karen.miles@medisys.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: peak-load SLA exhibit for pilot order form

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looks promising. We have a procurement question from engineering and legal: for our pilot and potential enterprise order, we need an addendum that covers peak-load handling during scheduled campaign windows and a clear credit schedule for temporary capacity shortages. Specifically: 

- We run 2–4 campaign surges per week with short bursts of high concurrency (20–30x baseline).
- We need a grace/failover policy when latency exceeds 700ms p95 for more than 15 minutes in a rolling 1-hour window.
- Requirement for regional failover sequencing (primary region us-west, secondary us-east) and notification windows.

Attached is our RFP section (Medisys_RFP_SLA.pdf). Can Redwood propose order form language (exhibit) and a short evidence plan for capacity guarantees? Also copying legal (Karen) who will review any language.

Appreciate a quick path forward — our procurement kickoff is next Tuesday.

Best,
Sophia
[Attachment: Medisys_RFP_SLA.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Li <sophia@medisys.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: peak-load SLA exhibit for pilot order form

Hi Sophia —

Thanks for the detail and the RFP. We can definitely put forward a peak-load SLA exhibit and a practical evidence plan. High level proposal:

- Peak-load exhibit that defines a "campaign surge" as a sustained concurrency uplift >10x baseline for a period >5 minutes and provides a burst-capacity policy (guaranteed baseline + on-demand surge capacity subject to burst credits).
- Latency SLO: p95 latency target of 500ms under baseline. For documented surges, allow a temporary elevated threshold (700ms p95) for up to 30 minutes per surge without credit, with credits starting after 30 minutes in a rolling 1-hour window.
- Regional failover: automatic routing to secondary region within 90s for capacity loss, with notification timeline of 10 minutes (incident declared) and full post-incident report within 72 hours.

I'll draft order form language and a short operational evidence checklist (telemetry and canary plan). Looping in Priyom and David to validate: Priyom, can you confirm whether the 30-minute non-credit window is feasible from an ops and cost perspective? David — do we have a standard monitoring/telemetry pack we can reference for evidence?

I attached a quick starter doc with suggested language.

Thanks,
Sooj
[Attachment: proposed-peak-load-rider-v1.docx (DOCX, 15KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medisys peak-load SLA — ops feasibility

Sooj / David — quick take from infra: agreeable with the proposed approach provided we clarify two items in the exhibit:

1) Batching/queueing tolerance: during surge windows we will apply transient queueing up to 120s for lower-priority requests; the exhibit needs to call out request priority classes and expected degradation paths.
2) Billing for burst capacity: recommend a burst credit model (pre-purchased credits applied first, then pay-as-you-go at a higher rate). If Medisys expects continuous 20–30x surges, that becomes a capacity planning discussion and we should propose a dedicated capacity add-on.

I can add suggested text for both and a small telemetry snippet that exposes concurrency, queue depth, and p95 latency by region.

—Priyom

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Li <sophia@medisys.com>
Cc: Andrew Reynolds <andrew.reynolds@medisys.com>, Karen Miles <karen.miles@medisys.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: peak-load SLA exhibit for pilot order form

Hi Sophia — attaching an editable order form exhibit and a short evidence checklist. Key changes based on infra input:

- Added a Request Priority appendix (P0/P1/P2) and explicit queueing expectations (lower priority may see up to 120s queueing during surges).
- Clarified the credit trigger: credits start after 30 minutes of sustained breach in a rolling 1-hour window; individual surge pockets shorter than 30 minutes are considered tolerated events.
- Proposed a two-tier burst credit model (pilot credit pool + overage rate).

Please review and flag anything legal needs to redline. If you're comfortable, we can try to lock the exhibit for the pilot and include a clause that final enterprise capacity commitments will be revisited prior to expansion.

Attachments: orderform-redlines-blank.docx, proposed-peak-load-rider-v1.docx

Thanks,
Sooj
[Attachment: orderform-redlines-blank.docx (DOCX, 8KB)]

From: Karen Miles <karen.miles@medisys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Sophia Li <sophia@medisys.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: peak-load SLA exhibit for pilot order form

Sooj / Sophia — thanks for the draft. A few legal asks:

- We need clearer definitions for "sustained breach" and an objective telemetry source (API usage metrics from Redwood Console + daily CSV export) as the single source of truth.
- Add a maximum aggregate credit cap for the pilot (Medisys prefers a fixed cap to avoid unbounded liability on Redwood side).
- Please include a simple flow for dispute resolution (15 business days to open, 45 days to resolve) and an escalation contact list.

If Redwood agrees to the telemetry source and the cap language, we can expedite procurement. Can you add those items and return an updated exhibit?

—Karen

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Miles <karen.miles@medisys.com>, Sophia Li <sophia@medisys.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: peak-load SLA exhibit for pilot order form

Karen — welcome questions. We're okay with Redwood Console metrics + daily CSV export as the telemetry source; I'll add language that references the Console export as the primary evidence and a runbook for how to request raw telemetry. For the pilot cap — propose a $15,000 aggregated credit cap tied to the pilot order value, with a review clause before expansion.

I'll update the exhibit to: 1) include explicit definitions (sustained breach = p95 latency > 700ms for >30m in a rolling 1-hour window), 2) include the Console CSV as the evidence source and the dispute timeline you requested, and 3) add the $15k cap for pilot credits. Expect the redline back within the day.

Thanks — Sooj

[Attachment: proposed-peak-load-rider-v2.docx (DOCX, 18KB)]
